h: A beach town, a mayor who won't close the water and three mismatched men on a boat; the shark barely shows and the dread never lets up.

like.r: The source novel, with more small-town politics and a grimmer cast, though the film trims the soap and keeps the sea.
Another monster picking off a cornered crew, with the same patient reveal-little, scare-a-lot approach but in space.
A group stuck with a predator they cannot see coming, colder and nastier than the sunny-beach menace here.

t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
h: A charming troublemaker fakes insanity to dodge prison and starts a war of wills with a ward's smiling, iron-fisted head nurse.

like.t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
like.r: The novel is narrated by the silent Chief, giving the same fight a stranger, more hallucinatory inside view.
Another story of an unruly man ground down by an institution that calls its cruelty treatment.
Another psychiatric ward as a society of misfits, with a young woman's view in place of a rebel's.

h: A bank robbery in the Brooklyn heat goes comically wrong and turns into a street circus, with a desperate man the crowd starts cheering.

like.r: The same grimy 1970s New York and a lone man cracking in public, but far lonelier and more menacing.
Lumet's other raw New York true story, with a cop standing alone against his own department.
A modern New York bank standoff where nobody is quite who they seem and the negotiation is the show.

t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
h: King Arthur's knights ride imaginary horses through a muddy Middle Ages of killer rabbits, pedants and sketches that break the fourth wall.

like.r: The same troupe's other classic, more pointed and satirical, with religion and revolutionaries as the target.
A warmer, gentler fairy-tale spoof that likewise loves its heroes while teasing every convention.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: British absurdist comedy with the same deadpan logic and a cheerful contempt for dignity, set among the stars.

h: An Irish rogue climbs the ranks of 18th-century Europe in candlelit tableaux; a picaresque told with the cool distance of a painting.

like.r: Another social climber's rise and fall narrated with irony by an author who judges everyone and forgives no one.
A similarly lavish period piece about status and appearances, with cruelty hidden in drawing-room manners.
Another bawdy 18th-century picaresque, but a brisk comedy where Kubrick is melancholy and still.

h: Twenty-four strangers drift through five days of country music and a presidential campaign in overlapping conversations and songs.

like.r: Altman again juggling a whole city of intertwined lives, this time in Los Angeles and drawn from Raymond Carver.
Another sprawling web of damaged people converging on one night, louder and more melodramatic.
A sharper, meaner Altman satire of an industry, with the same drifting camera and overlapping talk.

h: An insomniac cabbie cruises a filthy New York at night, his loneliness curdling into a mission; hypnotic, ugly and hard to look away from.

like.r: Another Scorsese portrait of a man whose rage and insecurity wreck everything near him.
The literary ancestor of the bitter, isolated narrator who stews in his own justifications.
A modern night-city loner whose chilling single-mindedness is played with the same unsettling charisma.

h: A small-time Philadelphia club fighter gets one shot at the title; mostly a shy love story and a hymn to going the distance.

like.r: The brutal other side of boxing movies, where the ring reveals a man instead of lifting him.
Avildsen's other underdog classic, with a mentor and a training montage in place of a boxing gym.
Another small, human boxing drama about a fighter and the old coach who believes in her, but far sadder.

h: A newsman has an on-air breakdown and the ratings soar, so the network decides madness sells; furious speeches and bleak office comedy.

like.r: An older, equally cynical drama about a journalist who exploits a tragedy for a bigger story.
A lighter satire of the same idea, where media can manufacture a reality for the public.
The same ratings-hungry news machine seen from the freelancer at the bottom, played as a chilly thriller.

h: Two reporters chase phone calls and unnamed sources until a burglary becomes a presidency; gripping despite being mostly typing and talking.

like.r: The reporters' own account, with more of the dead ends and the slog that the film compresses.
The modern heir: a newsroom team chasing a buried story through records, interviews and doors that stay shut.
Another procedural in which obsessive paper-chasing is the drama, set in a newsroom and darker in outcome.

h: A farm boy, a smuggler and a princess against a planet-sized empire; space opera built from samurai films, serials and myth.

like.r: The samurai adventure that gave Lucas his bickering pair of commoners escorting a royal through enemy land.
A weightier, more political desert epic about a young heir and a prophecy, for readers who want the myth with more depth.
Lucas's other serial throwback, with a whip-cracking archaeologist in place of a farm boy.

t: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
h: An ordinary man sees lights in the sky and can't stop building a mountain in his living room; awe and obsession, with aliens as a gift.

like.r: Spielberg's other alien visit, this time a child's friendship story that trades obsession for tenderness.
Another first-contact story that cares more about wonder and faith than invasion.
A quieter, more cerebral first contact that shares the hush and the emotional payoff.

h: A neurotic comedian dissects why his relationship with a sunny Midwesterner fell apart, talking straight to the camera.

like.r: Allen's black-and-white love letter to the city, with the same romantic muddle but a more rueful, less jokey tone.
Another New York romance built on talk, neuroses and a long friendship that keeps getting in love's way.
A black-and-white New York comedy of awkward people and fumbled relationships, with a young woman at the center.

h: A Brooklyn paint-store clerk becomes a king on the disco floor on Saturdays; the glitter hides a rougher story about going nowhere.

like.r: Another 1970s scene seen at its peak and its comedown, with a young nobody finding glory in a subculture.
A grittier take on the same working-class neighborhood with the same restless young men and a killer soundtrack.
A dance-floor romance that also hides class tension, but sunnier and more romantic.

h: A shy man in an industrial wasteland is handed a baby that won't stop crying; a nightmare in sound and shadow rather than a story.

like.r: Lynch's more accessible nightmare, with a mystery plot and a suburban surface cracking over the same weirdness.
Another stark black-and-white descent into one man's feverish, claustrophobic mind.
The silent ancestor of distorted sets and dream logic that shaped every nightmarish black-and-white film since.

h: Migrant workers and a dying landowner in the Texas wheat fields; a love triangle told through golden-hour light and a girl's wry voice-over.

like.r: Malick's debut, another dreamy American landscape with a young couple and a girl's detached narration.
Another stark American frontier story of greed and land, harsher and louder where this one is hushed.
A hazy, elegiac anti-western about ambition and love in a rough settlement, shot in a similar muted beauty.

h: Steelworkers from a Pennsylvania town go to Vietnam and come back changed; a long wedding, a hunt and a game with a gun.

like.r: A more direct Vietnam film that stays in the jungle where this one spends most of its time at home.
Another Vietnam epic, much more hallucinatory and operatic.
A book about the same war that asks what soldiers carry home, in linked stories of equal weight.

h: A summer fling reunites in a 1950s high school full of leather jackets, pink ladies and big dance numbers.

like.r: Another pastel 1960s teen musical with a bouncy score, but with a satirical edge about race and conformity.
Another sweet, sound-tracked romance across a class divide, with more heat and fewer pompoms.
A modern musical romance with the same bright showmanship, plus a bittersweet turn.

h: A farm boy from another world learns to fly and falls for a reporter; earnest, sunny and a template for every cape film since.

like.r: A much darker, gothic take on the comic-book hero, with a brooding city and a theatrical villain.
Another sincere hero origin story that puts the human life first and the powers second.
A funny, family-sized superhero adventure with the same big-hearted scale and old-fashioned optimism.

h: A captain journeys upriver through a hallucinating Vietnam to assassinate a colonel who has gone native; war as fever dream.

like.r: The novella Coppola transposed: a journey upriver into a moral abyss, shorter, more ironic and just as unsettling.
Another river journey into madness and ambition through a jungle that swallows its conquerors.
A colder, more clinical Vietnam picture about how war dehumanises, in two sharply different halves.

h: The crew of a hauling ship answers a distress call and brings something home; a haunted house in space with working-stiff dialogue.

like.r: Another cut-off crew facing a creature that can be anywhere, with more paranoia and less polish.
Scott's other lived-in future, a slower, melancholy noir with the same dirty, used-up look.
Another crew alone on a ship heading somewhere they should not, more philosophical and visually dazzling.

h: A TV writer's love life tangles with his friend's mistress and a teenage girlfriend, set to Gershwin in glowing black and white.

like.r: Allen's looser, jokier relationship comedy, where Manhattan trades some gags for a wistful, romantic mood.
Another New York web of couples and cheaters, warmer and more ensemble-driven.
An older New York comedy of lonely people and compromised love, equally bitter and tender.

h: A highway patrolman on collapsing Australian roads is pushed past the law by a motorcycle gang; low-budget, raw and very fast.

like.r: Another lean, low-budget dystopian action film with a world-weary loner and a ticking clock.
A bleaker, quieter dying world of roads and scavengers, trading the engines for a father and son.
The cop-turned-avenger template, with the same blurred line between justice and revenge.

h: A hapless man born next door to the Nativity is mistaken for a messiah in Roman Judea; a satire of zealots, bureaucrats and followers.

like.t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
like.r: The same troupe in a looser, sillier medieval romp that is less pointed and more silly.
Another great satire in which institutional madness runs the world, in black and white and blacker in tone.
Gilliam's own absurd satire of bureaucracy, with a darker and stranger vision.

h: A Coney Island gang must cross a hostile New York overnight to get home after a false accusation; a neon odyssey in one long night.

like.r: The grimmer source novel, modelled on Xenophon's Anabasis, with a far tougher view of street life.
Another gang story with a more romantic, tender view of the boys in it.
A neon-lit night-city chase film with a similar stylized cool and sparse dialogue.

h: A workaholic Broadway director rehearses a show and wrecks his body; a self-portrait that dances toward death with a grin.

like.r: The classic about a director whose life and film blur, which Fosse openly borrows from.
Fosse's other great musical, equally cynical and showy, with more of a political edge.
Another portrait of an artist consumed by perfectionism, with a mentor who drives him over the edge.

h: A workaholic ad man is abandoned with his young son and learns fatherhood by flailing; the custody fight is secondary to the breakfast scenes.

like.r: The modern version of the same divorce, with two sympathetic parents and lawyers making it worse.
Another quiet, heartbreaking family drama of a household that cannot talk to itself.
A broader, funnier take on a divorced father desperate to stay in his kids' lives.

h: A middleweight boxer wins in the ring and destroys everyone who loves him outside it; savage fights and jealousy in black and white.

like.r: The sunny, crowd-pleasing opposite: same sport, same city grit, but a man who wins at being decent.
Another Scorsese portrait of a volatile man, with the violence turned inward and into the street.
A raw, bruised look at a broken athlete trying to hold onto family and the only thing he does well.

h: The rebels scatter across ice, swamp and cloud, and the heroes lose more than they win; the space opera that grew up.

like.r: Another middle chapter that is darker and deeper than the film before it, about fathers, sons and the cost of power.

like.t: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
like.r: A larger-than-life quest with a similar mythic scale and a band of friends facing a shadowy empire.
A bigger, denser sci-fi saga of destiny, empire and a hero made by prophecy.

h: Two ex-cons in black suits reunite their band to save an orphanage, with soul legends and a record-breaking pile of wrecked cars.

like.r: Landis's rowdier earlier comedy with the same talent for escalating chaos and a cast of beloved slobs.
Another deadpan-comic Saturday Night Live alumni crew on a mission, with the supernatural for the stunts.
A goofier, more teenage-friendly music comedy built on the same affectionate silliness.

h: A horribly deformed man is rescued from a freak show by a surgeon in smoky Victorian London; a gentle, shadowy and heartbreaking drama.

like.r: An older, more unsettling story about sideshow outcasts and the cruelty of ordinary people toward them.
The classic about a gentle creature judged by his looks, told with more philosophy and fewer lamplit streets.
Lynch at his gentlest, another quiet, humane story with a very different kind of journey.

h: A tidy Illinois family is held together by silence after one son's death and the other's suicide attempt; therapy scenes quietly devastate.

like.r: The source novel, with more of the family's inner monologue than the film's restrained surface.
Another modern portrait of grief that refuses easy catharsis and finds humour in a bleak place.
Another cool, observant look at a repressed suburban family coming apart, with a colder lens on 1970s America.

h: An archaeologist with a whip races Nazis across the globe for a biblical relic; a serial-style chase built on perfect set pieces.

like.r: The same producer's pulp-serial playground, in space instead of the desert, with a similar rogue hero.
A lighter jungle adventure with a romance, a treasure and the same banter.
The Victorian ancestor of the treasure-hunting adventure, with a rugged hero and lost-world thrills.

h: Manhattan is a maximum-security prison island and an eyepatched outlaw has twenty-two hours to rescue the president from it.

like.r: A grimy low-budget action film in a collapsing near future, with an equally laconic hero.
Another dark, rain-and-neon vision of the future with a weary, noir-style anti-hero.
Another one-night odyssey through a hostile New York, filmed with the same lean pulp attitude.

h: Two British sprinters, one driven by faith and one by prejudice, head for the 1924 Olympics; stirring and unashamedly sincere.

like.r: Another underdog sports story with a triumphant score and a sincere hero.
Another very British true story of private struggle and public duty, with a gentle drive.
A more American underdog tale of one man's stubborn determination, as warm and just as sentimental.

h: A boy joins six dwarf thieves with a stolen map of time holes and meets Napoleon and Robin Hood; a children's adventure with a bitter streak.

like.r: Gilliam's darker, adult vision of the same bureaucratic absurdity, on a bleak future Earth.
A friendlier fairy-tale adventure with similar wit and a nostalgic, bedtime-story feel.
Another time-hopping romp through history, goofier and with a lot less menace.

h: A sound man recording wind noise captures a car crash and a gunshot, and spends the film trying to prove it; paranoia in Philadelphia.

like.r: The paranoid sound-recordist classic that De Palma was riffing on, quieter and more cerebral.
The photographer version of the same story, in which a recording seems to hold a murder.
The master-class in voyeurism and thriller craft that De Palma loves to quote.

h: A burnt-out cop hunts rogue replicants through a rainy, neon future Los Angeles; film noir that asks what makes a person real.

like.t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
like.r: The source novel, stranger and smaller, with more about animals, empathy and faith.
The founding cyberpunk novel, with the same rain-slick street-level future and noir plot.
Scott's other grimy future, a tense and tightly built horror in space.

h: A lonely suburban boy hides a stranded alien in his closet; a child's-eye friendship story that earns its tears.

like.t: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
like.r: Spielberg's earlier take on visitors from the sky, more awestruck and less of a family film.
Another film that holds a child's friendships and fears at eye level, warm and aching.
A rowdier 1980s kid adventure with the same Spielberg-produced sense of wonder and a bunch of friends.

h: A difficult out-of-work actor lands a soap role by becoming a woman and learns more than he planned; a farce with a heart.

like.r: The classic cross-dressing farce that set the template, in black and white and with sharper jokes.
Another man in disguise who learns to see the world differently, broader and more family-minded.
Another sharp, New York-centred adult comedy about love and neuroses.

h: A year in a California high school and its mall: crushes, bad jobs, a stoned surfer, and a surprisingly frank look at teen life.

like.r: Another loose, soundtrack-heavy, day-in-the-life teen ensemble, set in 1976 Texas.
A neater, more earnest teen comedy that talks about the same social cliques.
The cruder, later descendant about two friends hoping to make a memorable end to high school.

h: Three hours trace a London-trained lawyer who turns nonviolence into a weapon against an empire; reverent, sweeping and epic in scale.

like.r: Another sweeping British-Empire epic about one man and a foreign people, with more ambiguity and more sand.

like.t: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
like.r: Gandhi's own account of his life and principles, plainer and more self-critical than the film.
Another epic biography of a leader of a movement, angrier and focused on a very different struggle.

h: A hacker is zapped into a mainframe and forced into gladiator games on glowing grids; groundbreaking computer graphics and neon style.

like.r: The later, more philosophical film about a hacker discovering a digital world with its own rules.
Another 1980s computer fantasy where a clever kid and a machine come close to ending everything.
A big, playful quest inside a virtual world, with a video-game and pop-culture nostalgia.

h: A drifting Vietnam veteran is hassled by a small-town sheriff and takes to the mountains; leaner and sadder than its macho legacy suggests.

like.r: The novel is much bleaker and more violent, with a different ending and an equal sympathy for both men.
Another study of a damaged veteran who cannot rejoin a society that fears him.
A tighter, more fun 1980s lone-hero action movie that loses the trauma and keeps the suspense.

h: A Cuban refugee shoots, snorts and bullies his way to a Miami cocaine empire; excessive, profane and gleefully operatic.

like.r: The cooler, more dignified gangster saga that Scarface blows up into a loud, neon tragedy.
Another rise and fall of a hungry outsider in crime, faster, funnier and more lived-in.
The same 1980s greed-is-good appetite in a boardroom instead of a drug empire.

h: A Chicago-suburb kid left home alone for the weekend turns the house into a brothel; a slick, dreamy satire of ambition and money.

like.r: Another suburban kid pulling off an elaborate scam while his parents are away, much sunnier.
The earlier classic of a drifting, comfortable young man led astray by older temptations.
The poisoned, darker view of the same 1980s materialism, played as satire.

h: A teenage hacker dials into a military computer thinking it's a game and nearly starts a nuclear war; Cold War anxiety as a thriller.

like.r: The darkly funny version of the same fear of a nuclear catastrophe set off by systems and men.
Another early-1980s computer fantasy, more visual and less about suspense.
Another 1980s fear of machines taking over, with a hard-edged action thriller feel.

h: Two commodities tycoons bet a dollar on swapping a snobbish broker and a street hustler; a wicked Christmas class comedy.

like.r: The classic switched-lives story that this film updates with sharper edges.
Another Eddie Murphy comedy about a fast-talker in a world of the rich, more of an action film.
The serious, snarling version of the same 1980s world of traders and fortunes.

h: Test pilots and the first astronauts race the Soviets into space; a hearty, sprawling and sometimes comic look at the macho nerve it took.

like.r: The source book, with Wolfe's sparkling, mocking prose and deeper portraits of the pilots.
Another true space adventure, more focused on one crisis and one crew.
A quiet, grief-soaked take on the same era's space race, a contrast to this film's swagger.

h: A mockumentary about a man who physically becomes whoever he stands next to, spliced into real 1920s newsreels.

like.r: The other great fake-documentary comedy of the era, broader and set in rock, not in history.
Another ordinary man digitally inserted into famous moments in history, sweeter and less satirical.
Allen's most beloved comedy, warmer and with a much more romantic subject.

h: A prickly mother and her daughter bicker through decades of marriages, affairs and an ex-astronaut neighbor; a comedy that becomes a weeper.

like.r: Another mother-daughter comedy that turns to illness, with a more Southern, ensemble feel.
Another Oscar-winning family drama of the era that's colder and more restrained.
Brooks's later comedy-drama with another cranky loner who gets drawn into other people's lives.

h: A 1940s Indiana boy plots to get a BB gun for Christmas; a string of dry-eyed, nostalgic anecdotes narrated by the grown-up him.

like.r: Another film narrated by the adult version of the kid we watch, with a more bittersweet tone.
Another family Christmas favourite, more slapstick and less nostalgic.
Another warm string of childhood memories from a vanished era, narrated by the grown man looking back.

h: Poor greasers and rich Socs fight in 1960s Tulsa; a golden-hour, gloriously sincere teenage melodrama with a very famous cast.

like.r: The novel, written by a teenager, is plainer and closer to the boys' voices than the film's glow.
Another film of young friendships and loss, from a different angle with a lighter tone.
The 1950s original of the angry, tender teenage-outsider movie that this one echoes.

h: An unstoppable killer machine and a haggard soldier arrive in 1984 Los Angeles from the future, both after one waitress; lean, grimy and relentless.

like.r: Cameron's next step, a bigger and louder film that keeps the sense of a pursuing, implacable threat.
Another rainy, noir-edged future about humans and their man-made doubles, much more reflective.
Another time-travel story set in the 1980s, with the same cleverly looped plot but a sunnier mood.

h: Three out-of-work parapsychologists start a ghost-removal business in New York; deadpan wisecracks on top of a real apocalyptic threat.

like.r: Another big Saturday Night Live-era comedy with a wise-guy gang on an improbable mission.
Another comedy that treats the afterlife as an annoying bureaucracy, stranger and more gothic.
Another deadpan agents-versus-the-unknown comedy set in a secret New York.

h: A bitter court composer narrates how he destroyed the vulgar genius he could hear but never match; envy set to Mozart.

like.r: The stage play it came from, tighter and more theatrical, with the same duel between mediocrity and genius.
A modern portrait of music as obsession and rivalry, played at a pace and in a rhythm that hurts.
Another sumptuous 18th-century period piece, colder and more detached in tone.

h: A documentary crew follows a clueless British heavy-metal band on a disastrous American tour; the original mockumentary, deadpan to the end.

like.r: Another fake-documentary comedy, quieter and aimed at celebrity and history instead of rock.

like.t: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy
like.r: Another comedy that treats a self-important entertainer's idiocy with a straight face.
A warmer, sincere look at the same rock-tour world and its egos.

h: A mute drifter walks out of the Texas desert and slowly reclaims his son and his past; wide landscapes and Ry Cooder slide guitar.

like.r: Another quiet, spare portrait of drifting through the American West, with a documentary-like feel.
Another gentle journey across America to reconnect with family, equally slow and moving.
Another film that paints the American landscape as a character, more poetic and less personal.

h: A Texas bar owner hires a killer to dispose of his wife and her lover, and every misunderstanding after that makes things worse.

like.r: The Coens' later crime farce, in which an ordinary scheme spirals out of control, wryer and snowier.
Another tense Texas hunt where a bad decision follows a man everywhere, more fatalistic.
The hardboiled novel of an adulterous plot against a husband, the template for this kind of noir.

h: A motor-mouthed Detroit cop goes to Beverly Hills to avenge a friend and runs rings around the local police; Eddie Murphy at his peak.

like.r: Another 1980s buddy-cop hit that mixes banter and action, with more bruised heroes.
Murphy's earlier comic romp, a more satirical story of class lines crossed.
Brest's other buddy comedy-thriller, a road trip with a bounty hunter and a runaway accountant.

h: A bullied teen finds a mentor in a quiet handyman who teaches him karate through chores; the training-montage underdog template.

like.r: The same director's earlier underdog classic, gritty and adult where this is kid-sized.
A feel-good sports story of a young person fighting for a place in their sport.
Another mentor-and-student story with much darker, more punishing training.

t: Once Upon a Time in America
h: Four years of friendship among Jewish Lower East Side gangsters come back in an old man's opium haze; a long, mournful crime elegy.

like.r: Another sweeping American crime saga, with a stronger focus on a family and its power.
A quicker, funnier and more frenzied life in the mob, without the dreamy sadness.

like.t: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
like.r: Leone's earlier epic, with the same widescreen patience and operatic music, in the Old West.

h: A girl's sixteenth birthday is forgotten by her family amid her sister's wedding, while she pines after a senior; John Hughes's debut.

like.r: Another Hughes-written teen romance about class and crushes, with a slightly sadder edge.
A sweeter, more sincere teen romance with a famous boombox scene.
A later teen comedy with sharp dialogue and a generous heart toward its heroine.

h: A duke's son lands on a desert planet that holds the universe's most precious spice; baroque, strange and overstuffed.

like.r: The novel behind it, which makes the politics and ecology clear in ways the film cannot.
A modern, cleaner and grander rendering of the same story, less odd and more austere.
A lighter, more adventurous space opera that borrows desert planets and a chosen one.

h: A teen is flung back to 1955 and must make sure his parents fall in love; a time-travel comedy with a perfect clockwork plot.

like.r: Another 1980s time-travel story with a tightly looped plot, rewritten as a chase thriller.
Another high-concept comedy of a man stuck in time, which turns on a more emotional hinge.
A novel that sends a man to the past to change events, with a similar love of period detail and small-town charm.

h: Five teen stereotypes stuck in Saturday detention talk, fight and confess until the labels crack; one library, no escape.

like.r: A looser and raunchier ensemble view of the same teen world.
Hughes's lighter, more fantastical high-school film about escape.
Another single-room drama in which strangers are forced to talk until their prejudices crack.

h: A timid clerk in a paperwork-choked totalitarian bureaucracy dreams of flying, then tries to fix one clerical error; sad, funny and baroque.

like.r: The dystopian classic Gilliam turns into black comedy, with the same fear but a much grimmer tone.
Another black comedy about institutions that run on idiocy and procedure.
The original nightmare of faceless authority and arbitrary guilt that this film is heir to.

h: A gang of kids with a pirate map race a family of crooks through booby-trapped caves to save their neighborhood.

like.r: Another bunch of 1980s kids on a day-long quest, quieter and more touching.
The grown-up cousin: the same booby traps and treasure hunts with a whip-wielding professional.
Another Spielberg-produced suburban kids' adventure, with a warmer heart and an alien.

h: A Philadelphia detective hides in an Amish farming community to protect a boy who saw a murder; a thriller that falls into a gentle romance.

like.r: Weir's later, more inspirational drama about a closed community and one questioning voice.
Another crime story set in a gentle rural world where violence feels jarring.
A less romantic but equally tight thriller where an injured man is trapped in an isolated place.

h: A Danish baroness runs a Kenyan coffee farm and falls for a free-spirited hunter; sweeping landscapes, wistful voice-over and Barry's score.

like.r: Dinesen's own memoir, more reflective and less romantic than the film, written with great lyric skill.
Another sweeping, melancholy romance across an exotic landscape, with a more tragic, layered structure.
A grander epic of an outsider in a colonial landscape, with far more war and far less love.

h: A prim young Englishwoman in Florence is kissed in a field, then goes home to a safe engagement; Edwardian manners and repressed longing.

like.r: The gently ironic source novel, with the same comedy of manners and a yearning for a freer way to live.
Ivory's deeper, more melancholy Forster adaptation about class and inheritance.
The great comedy of manners in which a clever woman sees through convention in the end.

h: Can men and women just be friends? Twelve years of run-ins, breakups and Nora Ephron one-liners in an autumnal New York.

like.r: The neurotic New York romance that Ephron and Reiner borrowed from, drier and less sentimental.
Ephron's own follow-up rom-com with the same warm banter and a more fairy-tale spirit.
Another film about two people talking their way into love, quieter and set over a single night.

h: An unconventional English teacher persuades the boys of a strict New England prep school to seize the day; rousing, then devastating.

like.r: Another story about a mentor who sees a gifted young person's potential, with a modern, working-class setting.
Another film about young friendships that changes the lives of boys, with a far less formal setting.
A short novel of a New England boys' school, friendship and a tragic accident, with a quieter tone.

h: A respected doctor arranges a murder and tries to live with it while a documentary filmmaker fumbles his own life in a godless New York.

like.r: The great novel of a murder and its aftermath, which Allen turns into a modern, cynical question of conscience.
Allen's later retelling of the same idea, in London, with less comedy and a colder tone.
Allen's warmer ensemble drama, with the same interlocking stories but a gentler view of people.

h: A volunteer arrives in a Vietnam jungle and is caught between two sergeants, one decent and one savage; war from the mud level.

like.r: A colder, more stylized Vietnam picture that follows recruits from training to Hue.
A far more hallucinatory take on the same war, a journey into nightmare.
Another film that puts the soldier's-eye horror of a war front and center.

h: Ripley returns to the planet with a colony of marines who think they are bulletproof; a war movie with a mother's fury inside.

like.r: The slow, dread-filled original, which builds fear with shadows where this film builds it with firepower.
Another 1980s action film in which a tough squad realizes it is the prey, in a jungle.
Cameron's earlier lean thriller, with another relentless creature and a woman who becomes a fighter.

h: A charming Chicago senior fakes sick, borrows a Ferrari and drags his friends around the city; he talks right to the camera.

like.r: Hughes's more serious teen film, where a day of confinement cracks the same cliques.
Another day of suburban teenage rule-breaking, slicker and edgier.
A later, cruder comedy about the same teenage friendships and one wild night.

h: A college boy finds a severed ear in a field and is drawn into a sadistic criminal underworld hidden under a pastel American town.

like.r: Lynch's rawer and stranger early film, a nightmare with almost no plot.
Lynch's other hallucinatory mystery of a bright surface hiding a darker truth, set in Hollywood.
A classic of obsession and mistaken identity, a clear ancestor of Lynch's dream-noir.

h: Four twelve-year-old boys walk the railroad tracks to see a dead body, and talk about everything else; a writer remembers the summer.

like.r: The novella behind the film, with more of the narrator's later life and the same sharp feel for boyhood talk.
A rowdier, lighter 1980s film of kids on a quest, without the elegy.
A longer, quieter chronicle of growing up and the friendships and moments that stay with you.

h: Hotshot navy pilots, a volleyball game and a chorus of synth guitars; a glossy flight-school fantasy that sells the sky.

like.r: Scott and Cruise again, with race cars in place of jets and the same gleaming, fast excitement.
Another military-school romance with a cocky trainee and a stern instructor, though more earnest.
Another adrenaline-soaked buddy film of danger and brotherhood, this time with surfers and bank robberies.

h: Three sisters, their husbands and lovers circle one another across two Thanksgivings in New York; Allen's warmest ensemble comedy.

like.r: Allen's colder, darker companion piece on conscience and betrayal.
A vast ensemble of overlapping lives, more sprawling and satirical than this tight family circle.
The classic of sisters' bonds and loves, a century and a half earlier and much gentler.

h: A blustering truck driver stumbles into a sorcerer's war under San Francisco's Chinatown; a kung-fu fantasy comedy that mocks its own hero.

like.r: Carpenter's drier, more grim action fantasy with another gruff hero who fumbles his way through.
Another pulp adventure in a world of mystical threats, more polished and less silly.
Another 1980s comic fantasy where ordinary guys fight supernatural forces and bicker as they do.

h: A Brooklyn artist juggles three suitors and refuses to choose; Spike Lee's low-budget debut, sexy, funny and direct to the camera.

like.r: Lee's bigger, angrier Brooklyn film, with the same neighborhood and a much higher temperature.
Another New York relationship comedy that talks to the audience, from a very different perspective.
Another black-and-white shoestring debut full of talk and local characters.

h: A grandfather reads a boy the tale of a farm girl, a pirate, a giant and a vengeful swordsman; a fairy tale that mocks and means it.

like.r: The source novel, which pretends to be an abridgment and is even funnier and more cynical.

like.t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
like.r: A much sillier, more cynical medieval spoof with the same love of absurd dialogue.
A later romantic fairy-tale adventure with a similar wink and a hearty dose of villains.

h: Marine recruits are broken down by a screaming drill sergeant, then dropped into Vietnam; two halves, one icy view of what war does.

like.r: A more emotional and immediate Vietnam film, told from inside a platoon's moral divide.
A hallucinatory Vietnam epic where Kubrick is cold and exact.
The classic war novel of absurd institutions and black humor, in a different war.

h: An ambitious young broker is seduced by a charismatic corporate raider who preaches greed; a 1980s morality tale with slick suits.

like.r: A far wilder and funnier trip through the later excesses of the trading world.
A bleak, talky drama of desperate salesmen with the same ruthless view of business.
The same 1980s greed in a drug lord's mansion instead of an office.

h: A murdered Detroit cop is rebuilt as a corporate machine and starts to remember himself; ultraviolence under a razor-sharp media satire.

like.r: A more brooding, philosophical look at a manufactured being and what it means to be human.
Another relentless 1980s machine-as-cop story, played for dread and not for satire.
Verhoeven's later gory satire disguised as a military sci-fi action film.

h: A team of elite commandos in a Central American jungle realizes something invisible is picking them off; muscle turned into a horror hunt.

like.r: Another team of tough fighters against a monster, with more sci-fi and a clearer heart.
McTiernan's next film, a cleverer, more human action thriller in a single skyscraper.
Another cut-off group stalked by something that can look like anything, with more paranoia.

h: A petty crook and a cop, unable to have a baby, steal one of a furniture tycoon's quintuplets; a cartoonish southwestern farce.

like.r: The Coens' other slacker comedy of errors with another set of odd characters and quotable lines.
Another Coens comedy of drawling fugitives in a tall-tale South, with a bluegrass sound.
The Coens' grim debut, in which Texas crime goes far worse than it does here.

h: A sheltered girl at a Catskills resort learns to dance, and to see her own world, from the resort's rough-edged instructor.

like.r: The earlier dance-floor drama, grittier and in Brooklyn, with a fine soundtrack of its own.
Another sing-along period romance across social lines, goofier and more of a musical.
A newer romance powered by music and dance, with a bittersweet turn.

h: Two unemployed, hard-drinking actors flee squalid 1969 Camden for a rain-soaked cottage in the country; a cult comedy of grim, grand misery.

like.r: Another British cult comedy of friends and substances, faster and much more dangerous.
A British comic novel of misfits, humiliations and bitter wit that anticipates this film's mood.

like.t: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
like.r: Another two-man binge, set in America and a far more hallucinatory vision.

h: A privileged English boy is separated from his parents in occupied Shanghai and grows up in an internment camp; war seen through awed eyes.

like.r: The semi-autobiographical novel, colder and stranger in voice than Spielberg's lyrical film.
Spielberg's more harrowing World War II drama, with a grown man at its center.
Another film that shows a camp through a child and the adult who tries to protect him.

h: A barefoot New York cop is trapped in an LA skyscraper with a team of terrorists on Christmas Eve; the blueprint for the single-location action movie.

like.r: Another wise-cracking 1980s cop action film, with a buddy pair in place of one lone hero.
A later action thriller that follows Die Hard's model: one confined setting and a clever villain.
McTiernan's earlier action film, a more macho jungle hunt.

h: A hustling yuppie discovers his dead father's fortune went to an autistic brother he never knew and drags him on a cross-country drive.

like.r: Another odd-couple road trip of the same year, faster and more comic.
Another film that uses a gentle outsider's perspective to soften a cynical world.
Levinson's other character-led crowd-pleaser, this one a comedy with a manic performance.

h: A twelve-year-old wishes to be big and wakes up as a thirty-year-old, then thrives at a toy company by being the only adult who plays.

like.r: An older body-swap comedy that has a similar premise of a young mind in an adult world.
Another sweet 1980s high-concept comedy where a kid is lost in the wrong time.
Another warm comedy built on an absurd disguise that exposes what matters.

h: Two dead homeowners hire a foul-mouthed freelance ghost to scare away the awful new family; a macabre, gleeful afterlife farce.

like.r: Another ghosts-as-comedy blockbuster, more broadly crowd-pleasing and less gothic.
Burton's tender suburban fairy tale, sharing the pastel-and-shadow look but a far gentler tone.
Another macabre 1988 comedy with a very dark sense of humor, about teenagers and not ghosts.

h: A teenage girl and her charming psychopath boyfriend start killing the cruel clique that rules her school and disguising it as suicide.

like.r: The lighter, safer descendant of the same school-clique satire, with the murder replaced by gossip.
The sincere 1980s take on teen cliques, which this film wickedly sends up.
Another stylized black comedy of youthful violence and invented slang, much harsher.

h: Thieves double-cross each other over a diamond heist, a barrister falls for the con woman and a stutterer takes revenge; British farce with American bite.

like.t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
like.r: Cleese's earlier British comedy, wilder and more surreal than this tightly plotted farce.
An Ealing comedy of crooks undone by their own mishaps, from the same school of British black comedy.
Another 1980s ensemble comedy full of schemes, double-crosses and a satisfying comeuppance.

h: The hottest day of the summer on one Brooklyn block, where small slights and a pizzeria wall of fame build toward a flash point.

like.r: Lee's looser, funnier first film in the same neighborhood, with a very different temperature.
Lee's epic on the activist, the political side of the questions this film asks about protest and violence.
Another film that grounds the story in a single neighborhood and its pressures, in South Central Los Angeles.

h: A brooding millionaire in a bat suit takes on a grinning gangster in a gothic Gotham; the comic-book film that made superheroes dark.

like.r: The sunny, earnest superhero film that Burton's brooding picture turned upside down.
A later, grittier and more realistic Batman, with a bigger focus on crime and chaos.
Burton's comic gothic from the year before, with the same nightmare-storybook design.
